encounters.cc: Chronic diarrhea, abdominal bloating, and unintentional weight loss

lines: Chronic diarrhea, abdominal bloating, and unintentional weight loss

The patient is a 28-year-old female with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus, Celiac disease diagnosed in January 2020, and iron deficiency anemia diagnosed in March 2020, who returns for follow-up evaluation of persistent gastrointestinal complaints.
She reports that these symptoms have been present for the past year but have worsened over the last 4 months.
The diarrhea occurs 4–6 times per day, often within a few hours after meals, and is described as loose, bulky, and foul-smelling.
She notes increased bloating after eating pasta, bread, pastries, or certain breakfast cereals.
Over the past few months, she has also experienced frequent fatigue and difficulty concentrating.
She denies fevers, night sweats, or recent travel.
Her menstrual cycles are regular, but she has noticed heavier flow over the last several months.
She recalls having mouth sores intermittently over the past year, which she attributed to stress.
She has also experienced mild, diffuse bone pain on occasion and notes that her fingernails have become more brittle.
She has not changed her diet intentionally but has occasionally skipped meals due to bloating and discomfort.
She has tried over-the-counter probiotics and fiber supplements without improvement.
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro per sliding scale with meals
- Ibuprofen 400 mg orally every 6 hours as needed for menstrual cramps
Her family history is notable for a maternal aunt with “intestinal issues” and a cousin diagnosed with type 1 diabetes.
There is no family history of inflammatory bowel disease or colon cancer.
The patient works as a preschool teacher and lives with her partner.
She denies any recent sick contacts.
She has not been hospitalized and has not used antibiotics in the past year.
She has no pets and drinks municipal tap water.
She does not smoke or use alcohol or illicit drugs.
On review of systems, she denies rash, but on further questioning, she recalls a prior episode of a mildly itchy rash on her elbows about a year ago that resolved without treatment.
She has not had joint swelling, back pain, or visual changes.
She does not have any urinary symptoms or lower extremity swelling.
Temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure 108/66 mm Hg, pulse 78/min, and respirations 14/min.
On examination, the patient is alert and cooperative but appears thin.
Oral examination reveals a shallow, well-circumscribed ulcer on the left buccal mucosa.
The abdomen is mildly distended with hyperactive bowel sounds and diffuse, mild tenderness to palpation, greatest in the upper abdomen.
There is no hepatosplenomegaly or abdominal masses.
Extremities show no edema, and neurologic examination is normal.
Laboratory studies reveal a hemoglobin of 10.8 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume of 74 fL, and ferritin of 8 ng/mL.
Stool cultures and ova/parasite studies are negative.
An upper endoscopy is performed and shows a scalloped appearance of the duodenal mucosa.
